primary_sources: Google Web.dev Core Web Vitals Guidelines

rules.rule_name: Core Web Vitals Optimization (LCP, INP, CLS)
rules.explanation: Poor Core Web Vitals scores lead to high bounce rates, poor user experience, and heavily penalized search engine rankings.
rules.do: Optimize LCP (Largest Contentful Paint < 2.5s), INP (Interaction to Next Paint < 200ms), and minimize CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift < 0.1) using explicit dimensions and optimized asset delivery.
rules.dont: Do not insert un-sized dynamic elements that cause layout shifts or load unoptimized massive media assets above the fold.

rules.rule_name: Code Splitting and Route-Based Lazy Loading
rules.explanation: Shipping a single massive JavaScript bundle forces users to download unneeded code for hidden routes, causing slow initial page loads.
rules.do: Implement dynamic imports (e.g., React.lazy, dynamic import syntax) to split bundles along route boundaries and heavy UI widgets.
rules.dont: Do not import entire heavy libraries (e.g., lodash, moment) synchronously when sub-path imports or lighter alternatives exist.

rules.explanation: Uncompressed images and missing static asset caching headers consume unnecessary user bandwidth and slow render times.
rules.do: Serve modern image formats (AVIF/WebP) with responsive srcset attributes, utilize CDNs, and set aggressive Immutable Caching headers for static assets.
rules.dont: Do not serve raw, uncompressed PNG/JPEG files directly without responsive dimensions or caching strategies.

rules.explanation: Rendering thousands of inactive DOM elements simultaneously consumes massive browser memory and causes UI jank during scrolling.
rules.do: Virtualize long data lists (e.g., tanstack-virtual, react-window) so only visible rows/items reside in the active DOM tree.
rules.dont: Do not render unbounded arrays directly into the DOM tree without list pagination or window virtualization.
